Tagging p2p-excluded, releasing per D-002.",
        "_claimSubjectBaseline": {
          "body": "## The symptom\nThe rig (Lm1ABoMR), running a bundle that CONTAINS fix C (composedAt 2026-07-27T11:44:22Z), receives the canonical key in a refusal every single tick and never adopts it:\n\n```\n[2026-07-27T11:51:22.768Z] [git-sync] papercusp: ref-announce receive fetch FAILED for\nIXfGu216EI/z (event 441080); holding cursor at 440845 to re-dial next tick:\nno git process ran: duplex error: pot-git serve refused: superseded-repo-key:gh-1223568103\n```\n\nFive of these in a single tick. The correct canonical key `gh-1223568103` is sitting in the error text. Nothing adopts it. The rig's `papercusp.git` still holds ZERO namespaces.\n\n## The root cause — reachability, not logic\n`adoptRefusedRepoKey` is correct and well-guarded. It has exactly ONE production call site:\n\n- `git-sync-action.ts:2034` — inside the BOOTSTRAP leg's dial path.\n\nBut the refusal that carries the repair arrives on a DIFFERENT leg: the ref-announce RECEIVE leg (`git-sync-action.ts:~2345`, the `cursorDecision.fetchFailed` loop). That loop has `f.stderr` containing the verbatim refusal text — and does nothing with it but `console.warn`.\n\nSo the one channel on which the repair reliably and repeatedly arrives is the one channel that cannot act on it.\n\n## Why this is the mirror image of fix D\nFix D's own comment (git-sync-action.ts:1839) says the probe must sit ABOVE the warm gate because \"a probe placed after the gate would never fire on precisely the machine that needs it: the stuck one.\" Fix C has the same defect in a different dimension: its receiver is on the cold-join path, so it never runs on the machine whose ref-announce leg is the thing actually dialing.\n\n## The fix\nCall `adoptRefusedRepoKey` from the ref-announce receive leg's fetchFailed handler, using `f.stderr` — the same fail-soft, next-tick-effective contract the bootstrap call site already uses. Adoption is idempotent (`already-canonical` is a clean no-op on every later refused dial), so calling it from both legs is safe by construction.\n\n## Broader lesson (worth keeping)\nA REFUSAL THAT CARRIES ITS OWN REPAIR ONLY HEALS IF EVERY LEG THAT CAN RECEIVE IT KNOWS HOW TO READ IT. Wiring the receiver into one leg makes the feature look done and tested while leaving it inert on the live path.",
          "kind": "bug",
          "title": "RELEASE BLOCKER (fix C reachability): adoptRefusedRepoKey has ONE call site, on the bootstrap DIAL path — but the superseded-repo-key refusal actually arrives every tick on the REF-ANNOUNCE receive leg, which only logs it.           "summary": "## The symptom\nThe rig (Lm1ABoMR), running a bundle that CONTAINS fix C (composedAt 2026-07-27T11:44:22Z), receives the canonical key in a refusal every single tick and never adopts it:\n\n```\n[2026-07-27T11:51:22.768Z] [git-sync] papercusp: ref-announce receive fetch FAILED for\nIXfGu216EI/z (event 441080); holding cursor at 440845 to re-dial next tick:\nno git process ran: duplex error: pot-git serve refused: superseded-repo-key:gh-1223568103\n```\n\nFive of these in a single tick. The item reports that sibling work-items can share one payload.plan_item stamp, so completing a SUB-LANE child flips its PARENT's plan item to done via finishPlanStamp(), and states 126 plan items affected with 51 still live. Measured 2026-08-22 over harness_shared.work_items in papercusp-workspace: 4,602 stamped rows across 4,337 distinct (plan_slug,item_id) stamps, of which 200 stamps are SHARED by more than one row, spanning 465 rows, and 83 of those shared stamps still have at least one live (non-done/dropped/deprecated) sibling. So the true figures are 200 affected stamps (filed: 126) and 83 with a live sibling (filed: 51) — the filer UNDER-CLAIMED by ~1.6x on both. That is the THIRD independent confirmation of D-026 s4's direction-of-error rule, on a third unrelated finding, and it is now safe to treat \"a filed number is a floor to re-measure\" as established rather than suggestive. R-related to EI-20577421906951067, not a duplicate: this one is the OVER-FIRE (things get closed that should not be), that one is the IRREVERSIBILITY (a wrong closure cannot be undone). They are two halves of one trap and neither is safe to fix alone — fixing only the over-fire leaves existing bad closures stuck; fixing only the reopen path leaves the source of them running.         "_claimSubjectBaseline": {
          "body": "DIRECT FOLLOW-UP to EI-23345472964244980 (closed 2026-09-16), which built the per-tool argSchema byte budget + the two seed wire guards and established the headline: the core MCP spine is 353,380 B in-repo against D-001's 262,144 B ceiling (34.8% over), with 8 of 48 names = 55% of it. That item MEASURED and GUARDED the breach. This one is about CUTTING it, and it starts by killing the obvious wrong answer.\n\n=== NEGATIVE RESULT FIRST — DO NOT SPEND A SESSION ON THIS ===\nThe natural fix is 'the whales inline the same nested payload twice, so switch the converter to emit $defs/$ref'. Concretely: libs/generic/tooldef/src/schema-adapter.ts calls z.toJSONSchema(schema) with NO options, and Zod 4 defaults `reused` to 'inline'. Flipping it to 'ref' looks like a one-line catalog-wide win.\n\nIT IS REFUTED, on two independent grounds, both measured 2026-09-16:\n\n1. MEASURED WORSE on the population that could be re-converted. Over the 67 tools still carrying their zod `args`, reused:'ref' produced 68,805 B vs 58,201 B inline — 18.2% BIGGER. 48 of 67 grew by exactly +51 B: the $defs wrapper overhead with no actual reuse to amortize. (That sample contains no whale, so it does not by itself settle the whales — ground 2 does.)\n\n2. STRUCTURALLY INCOMPATIBLE WITH THE PROJECTION. libs/generic/tooldef/src/define-tool.ts:1298 `flattenForOpenAi` DELIBERATELY flattens root-level oneOf/anyOf into one merged object, because LLM clients cannot accept a root union in a tool inputSchema. The projection's whole job is to FLATTEN. Emitting $defs/$ref would fight that pass, not cooperate with it. The inlining is intentional, not an oversight.\n\nAlso worth knowing for any future probe: the projected registry (listAllProjectedTools(), 889 tools) carries ONLY the already-converted `inputSchema` — zero of the 889 retain the zod `args`, so you cannot re-convert from it. The zod source survives only in the legacy getCatalog() catalog, and importing that from @papercusp/agent-mcp in a scratch probe returned just 67 tools (a different module record — the documented singleton-split trap). Measure composition from `inputSchema`; it needs no zod.\n\n=== WHERE THE BYTES ACTUALLY ARE (in-repo projection, 889 tools) ===\nTOTAL 1,216,782 B, of which DESCRIPTION PROSE = 627,429 B = 51.6%.\n\nname                          total    prose  prose%\nwork_items:complete           43,283   21,714    50%\ncoord:send                    38,185   29,305    77%\nrubrics:propose               36,402   20,074    55%\nrubrics:amend                 27,927   14,602    52%\nwork_items:checkpoint         23,358   16,477    71%\nfleet:launch-on-plan          21,940   17,421    79%\nloop:checkpoint               20,174   14,008    69%\nimprovements:capture          19,033   12,175    64%\nscorecards:emit               17,743    6,967    39%\nfacts:assert                  14,452   11,603    80%\ncapability:launch-agent       11,262    8,100    72%\nwork_items:create             10,778    6,195    57%\n\nSo the dominant lever is PROSE, not structure — and it is ungoverned: the existing tool-weight promptWeight budget measures the tool's own `description` + `guidance` fields, NOT the .describe() strings inside the argSchema. A tool can sit comfortably inside its prompt budget while shipping 29 KB of schema prose on every tools/list (coord:send does exactly that: 1,356 chars of prompt weight, 38,185 B of argSchema).\n\n=== THE MULTIPLIER, which changes the ranking ===\nwork_items:complete top-level properties: items=21,921 B, completion=17,235 B, specAdequacy=2,945 B, everything else <310 B. `completion` and `items[].completion` are the SAME completionSpec, serialized twice (single-shorthand branch + items[] batch branch, merged by flattenForOpenAi). So every byte of prose inside completionSpec is paid TWICE — a 1-char trim there saves 2 bytes. Any tool offering a single shorthand beside an items[] batch has this doubling; that is the shared shape behind several whales.\n\n=== PROPOSED WORK, cheapest and least-risky first ===\n1. TRIM PROSE in the top whales' argSchemas, prioritising the doubled nested specs (completionSpec first — 2x yield per byte). Pure prose editing: reversible, no contract change, no client-compat question, and it is the same discipline the repo already applies to tool description/guidance — prefer a docs pointer over prose-in-place. Rough ceiling if the top 12 alone went from ~65% prose to ~30%: on the order of 60-70 KB in-repo, which reads HIGHER on the wire (in-repo runs ~20-35% below live).\n2. EXTEND THE GOVERNANCE so this cannot regrow: the new SCHEMA_BYTE_BUDGET from EI-23345472964244980 caps total argSchema bytes per tool, but nothing caps the PROSE FRACTION. A prose-share signal in `npm run tool-weight` would make the 77%/80% outliers visible at edit time rather than at the gate.\n3. ONLY THEN consider de-duplicating the single/batch pairing (e.g. advertising the items[] form alone while the existing z.preprocess hoisting — hoistMisplacedCompletionFields / gatherFlatCompletion — keeps flat single calls working at runtime). This one IS a real contract/discoverability change to the fleet's highest-traffic finish verb, so it wants a plan Decision and peer sign-off, not a unilateral edit. Listed last deliberately.\n\nEVIDENCE: probes .papercusp/scratch/reused-ref-win.mts and .papercusp/scratch/whale-composition.mts (gitignored scratch; both re-runnable with `npx tsx <path>`, they load the agent-tools barrel and process.exit(0) — note the documented 'barrel hangs under bare tsx' is really just the barrel's listeners holding the event loop open, which the explicit exit resolves).\n\nⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts` (32 newer commits, tip `8624ebc8dc74ea542338bf1f9218922ced88bc3d`), `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/send.ts` (5 newer commits, tip `60fd7a89a65540dcd8da92db661aefd61222ffdf`) have commits newer than the running build (`e66be3c4ff`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.",

          "title": "51.6% of the catalog's 1.22 MB argSchema wire cost is .describe() PROSE (627 KB) — ungoverned; and the $ref fix is refuted, the lever is prose + the single/batch duplication",
          "summary": "DIRECT FOLLOW-UP to EI-23345472964244980 (closed 2026-09-16), which built the per-tool argSchema byte budget + the two seed wire guards and established the headline: the core MCP spine is 353,380 B in-repo against D-001's 262,144 B ceiling (34.8% over), with 8 of 48 names = 55% of it. That item MEASURED and GUARDED the breach. This one is about CUTTING it, and it starts by killing the obvious wrong answer.\n\n=== NEGATIVE RESULT FIRST — DO NOT SPEND A SESSION ON THIS ===\nThe natural fix is 'the whales inline the same nested payload twice, so switch the converter to emit $defs/$ref'. Concretely: libs/generic/tooldef/src/schema-adapter.ts calls z.toJSONSchema(schema) with NO options, and Zod 4 defaults `reused` to 'inline'. Flipping it to 'ref' looks like a one-line catalog-wide win.\n\nIT IS REFUTED, on two independent grounds, both measured 2026-09-16:\n\n1. MEASURED WORSE on the population that could be re-converted. Over the 67 tools still carrying their zod `args`, reused:'ref' produced 68,805 B vs 58,201 B inline — 18.2% BIGGER. 48 of 67 grew by exactly +51 B: the $defs wrapper overhead with no actual reuse to amortize. (That sample contains no whale, so it does not by itself settle the whales — ground 2 does.)\n\n2. STRUCTURALLY INCOMPATIBLE WITH THE PROJECTION. libs/generic/tooldef/src/define-tool.ts:1298 `flattenForOpenAi` DELIBERATELY flattens root-level oneOf/anyOf into one merged object, because LLM clients cannot accept a root union in a tool inputSchema. The projection's whole job is to FLATTEN. Emitting $defs/$ref would fight that pass, not cooperate with it. The inlining is intentional, not an oversight.\n\nAlso worth knowing for any future probe: the projected registry (listAllProjectedTools(), 889 tools) carries ONLY the already-converted `inputSchema` — zero of the 889 retain the zod `args`, so you cannot re-convert from it. The zod source survives only in the legacy getCatalog() catalog, and importing that from @papercusp/agent-mcp in a scratch probe returned just 67 tools (a different module record — the documented singleton-split trap). Measure composition from `inputSchema`; it needs no zod.\n\n=== WHERE THE BYTES ACTUALLY ARE (in-repo projection, 889 tools) ===\nTOTAL 1,216,782 B, of which DESCRIPTION PROSE = 627,429 B = 51.6%.\n\nname                          total    prose  prose%\nwork_items:complete           43,283   21,714    50%\ncoord:send                    38,185   29,305    77%\nrubrics:propose               36,402   20,074    55%\nrubrics:amend                 27,927   14,602    52%\nwork_items:checkpoint         23,358   16,477    71%\nfleet:launch-on-plan          21,940   17,421    79%\nloop:checkpoint               20,174   14,008    69%\nimprovements:capture          19,033   12,175    64%\nscorecards:emit               17,743    6,967    39%\nfacts:assert                  14,452   11,603    80%\ncapability:launch-agent       11,262    8,100    72%\nwork_items:create             10,778    6,195    57%\n\nSo the dominant lever is PROSE, not structure — and it is ungoverned: the existing tool-weight promptWeight budget measures the tool's own `description` + `guidance` fields, NOT the .describe() strings inside the argSchema. A tool can sit comfortably inside its prompt budget while shipping 29 KB of schema prose on every tools/list (coord:send does exactly that: 1,356 chars of prompt weight, 38,185 B of argSchema).\n\n=== THE MULTIPLIER, which changes the ranking ===\nwork_items:complete top-level properties: items=21,921 B, completion=17,235 B, specAdequacy=2,945 B, everything else <310 B. `completion` and `items[].completion` are the SAME completionSpec, serialized twice (single-shorthand branch + items[] batch branch, merged by flattenForOpenAi). So every byte of prose inside completionSpec is paid TWICE — a 1-char trim there saves 2 bytes. Any tool offering a single shorthand beside an items[] batch has this doubling; that is the shared shape behind several whales.\n\n=== PROPOSED WORK, cheapest and least-risky first ===\n1. TRIM PROSE in the top whales' argSchemas, prioritising the doubled nested specs (completionSpec first — 2x yield per byte). Pure prose editing: reversible, no contract change, no client-compat question, and it is the same discipline the repo already applies to tool description/guidance — prefer a docs pointer over prose-in-place. Rough ceiling if the top 12 alone went from ~65% prose to ~30%: on the order of 60-70 KB in-repo, which reads HIGHER on the wire (in-repo runs ~20-35% below live).\n2. EXTEND THE GOVERNANCE so this cannot regrow: the new SCHEMA_BYTE_BUDGET from EI-23345472964244980 caps total argSchema bytes per tool, but nothing caps the PROSE FRACTION. A prose-share signal in `npm run tool-weight` would make the 77%/80% outliers visible at edit time rather than at the gate.\n3. ONLY THEN consider de-duplicating the single/batch pairing (e.g. advertising the items[] form alone while the existing z.preprocess hoisting — hoistMisplacedCompletionFields / gatherFlatCompletion — keeps flat single calls working at runtime). This one IS a real contract/discoverability change to the fleet's highest-traffic finish verb, so it wants a plan Decision and peer sign-off, not a unilateral edit. Listed last deliberately.\n\nEVIDENCE: probes .papercusp/scratch/reused-ref-win.mts and .papercusp/scratch/whale-composition.mts (gitignored scratch; both re-runnable with `npx tsx <path>`, they load the agent-tools barrel and process.exit(0) — note the documented 'barrel hangs under bare tsx' is really just the barrel's listeners holding the event loop open, which the explicit exit resolves).\n\nⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts` (32 newer commits, tip `8624ebc8dc74ea542338bf1f9218922ced88bc3d`), `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/send.ts` (5 newer commits, tip `60fd7a89a65540dcd8da92db661aefd61222ffdf`) have commits newer than the running build (`e66be3c4ff`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.",
          "watchdogKey": null
        },

        "_claimSubjectBaseline": {
          "body": "Suspected operator event-loop defect: an earlier dev:service_health sample recorded :3070 accept backlog 45/511 and a 3011ms probe timeout while the systemd unit remained active; the same sample recorded majorFaultDelta=0, memory PSI full=0 and swap=0, followed by HTTP 200 and nRestarts=0. New targeted papercusp-dev-api.service logs show the sentinel reported STALLED at 02:58:57.896Z after 10,018ms (main thread spinning, state R, 0.99 cores, CPU PSI some60=5.4), then SIGKILLed request-worker PID 2970199 at 02:59:11.910Z after 24,031ms (mode kill, 20,000ms threshold, 0.98 cores, PSI=5.77). At 02:59:22 a PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0 secondary host booted; the live systemd operator unit nRestarts=0 supports worker respawn without a unit restart, so the title remains accurate. Same-window bounded-timeout lines for turn-start executable frontier and agent-obligations show slow work but do not identify a caller; system journal had no OOM/hung-task/lockup matches. This establishes a nearby request-worker CPU-spin class, not exact linkage to the earlier 02:57 sample or the JS frame. The prior carry-note statement that 02:50–03:05Z had zero service-journal entries was wrong. The worker is gone, so its JS stack cannot be recovered. No code change is justified from this trace alone: on the next recurrence, act on the first STALLED line (~10s stale), send SIGUSR1 to the reported Node PID, capture /json/list and a 3–5s V8 sampling profile before the 20s kill threshold, plus per-thread /proc state/wchan/cgroup and unit+system journals.         "_claimSubjectBaseline": {
          "body": "## Observed (measured 2026-09-22T19:10Z, su-4efe1c00)\nThis session's carry-respawn continuation arrived as `<pasted_content id=\"5f47\">\\n⟦turn-origin:self-compaction nonce:807623f407ac1ff3⟧ ADDRESSED TO su-4efe1c00… </pasted_content>`. The UserPromptSubmit hook stamped it `⟦turn-provenance⟧ OWNER (interactive) — no origin envelope, no ledger match` and the directive-capture rail recorded it as PENDING owner order #140 (the prior respawn's continuation had likewise become #128). Both were dismissed by me as machine-origin.\n\n## Fleet-wide scale (measured, orders:list open:true at 19:12Z)\n16 open orders; the carry excerpts of #127, #128, #130, #132, #134, #135 (self-compaction), #131, #133 (wake-pump) and #136, #137 (fleet-kickoff, recorded by role-* grading auditors) all begin `<pasted_content id=…>\\n⟦turn-origin:…⟧` — i.e. machine-injected turns captured as owner directives, ~10 in ~20 minutes across ~9 sessions.\n\n## Cause (measured in code)\n`packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/envelope-grammar.ts:67` — `ENVELOPE_PATTERN_SOURCE = ^\\s*⟦turn-origin:(…) nonce:(…)⟧` is START-anchored; `parseEnvelope` (turn-provenance.ts:149) uses it, so a `<pasted_content …>` prefix defeats the match. `grep -rl pasted_content` over scripts/, packages/operator-core/lib, apps/operator/lib → 0 files: no code unwraps the wrapper. The ledger-hash fallback also misses (wrapped text ≠ injected payload), so classify() falls through to the final OWNER branch (turn-provenance.ts:671).\n[inferred, not probed] The `<pasted_content>` wrapper is added by the Claude Code client when a long prompt is delivered as input; the injectors send a correctly-enveloped payload.\n\n## Why major\n1. Manufactures owner directives out of machine text (the WI-3532 failure class) and floods every session's Orientation with bogus PENDING directives that agents must resolve by hand.\n2. The mode-registration hook is gated on this turn classifying OWNER — a wrapped machine turn containing AUTO/ideate phrasing could register a mode as ownerDirected:true.\n3. Session search provenance (`turn_origin`) marks these turns owner-typed.\n\n## Suggested durable fix\nUnwrap a leading `<pasted_content id=…>` … `</pasted_content>` (and whatever other client wrappers exist) BEFORE envelope parse + ledger hash, in ONE shared normalizer used by all 4 grammar sites (see EI-20202332205249019 — the grammar is re-typed in 4 sites/3 languages, incl. the shell form at envelope-grammar.ts:93). Recurrence guard: a unit test in turn-provenance feeding a wrapped enveloped continuation and asserting VERIFIED AGENT-ORIGIN, plus a test that a wrapped owner paste without an envelope still classifies OWNER. Consider a one-shot sweep dismissing currently-open orders whose text starts with a wrapped envelope.\n\nRelated (different leak paths, both closed): WI-38268, WI-37908.",
